crackers.detail: Under 21 CFR 101.4, ingredients are listed in descending order of predominance. tortilla_chips.detail: The step is nixtamalization: dry corn is soaked and cooked in a solution of slaked lime and water. Slaked lime is calcium hydroxide, called “cal.” The cooked corn, called nixtamal, is washed, then ground into a dough, masa. The word comes from Nahuatl, the Aztec language. Cornmeal from untreated corn cannot form a dough with water alone. Masa harina means “dough flour,” the powder ground from nixtamal. Masa flour made at scale is based on the traditional method. Restaurant-style chips are tortillas cut into wedges and fried. Most bagged chips are shaped straight from coarse masa dough and fried. For chips, Kristy’s standard is lard, tallow, coconut oil or olive oil. Skip seed oils; avocado oil fits only when the maker states it is pure and cold-pressed.

popcorn.detail: Popcorn is a variety of corn, Zea mays everta. Its hard outer hull is the pericarp. Inside, moisture runs about 13 to 14.5 percent of the kernel. As the water heats, the kernel acts as a pressure cooker until the hull ruptures. Kernels with cuts or weak spots in the hull let the moisture escape and stay unpopped. In one study, 4 to 47 percent of kernels failed to pop, depending on variety. Two popped shapes are grown, butterfly and mushroom. Mushroom popcorn is often sold prepopped and coated with flavorings. For popping at home, Kristy’s standard is coconut oil, butter or tallow. Skip seed oils; avocado oil fits only when the maker states it is pure and cold-pressed.

frozen_fries.detail: The federal grade standard describes frozen french fries as mature white potatoes, washed, sorted and trimmed. They may be cut or left whole. They are deep-fried or blanched in fat or oil, then frozen. Blanching is a short cook in hot water or steam. In a plant, the strips are peeled, cut and blanched, then par-fried, meaning partly fried, and frozen. Blanching also leaches sugars from the strips. The fries are finish-fried from frozen to develop color and crispness. Why it works: frying is first a dehydration process, meaning it drives water out of the food. The drier the food going in, the better the crust. So cooks fry once, freeze, and fry again. As food cools, moisture moves from the center to the surface. The second fry boils it off. The first fry also leaves simpler pathways inside, so water escapes more easily the second time. An air fryer is a convection appliance, meaning it circulates hot air. It cooks faster than an oven and gives a crisp outside. French fries cook well in one. For added fat, Kristy’s standard is tallow, olive oil, or coconut oil. Skip seed oils; avocado oil fits only when the maker states it is pure and cold-pressed. Look for thick-cut fries on the bag. Acrylamide forms during high-heat browning; it is a cooking byproduct, not an added ingredient.

Skip a waffle list naming Red 40, Yellow 5, Yellow 6 or Blue 1. Each is a synthetic dye, and a “Lake” dye still counts.

frozen_nuggets.detail: On poultry labels, “white meat” or “light meat” means 100 percent light meat. “Mostly white meat” means 66 percent or more light meat. “Natural proportions” means 50 to 65 percent light meat. A nugget is an irregular, usually bite-sized piece, usually breaded and fried, meant as finger food. “Chicken Nugget” with no qualifier means a solid piece of meat or poultry. “Chopped and Formed” beside the name means chopped and formed meat or poultry. With binders, extenders or water, “nugget” is only a fanciful name. A descriptive name then follows, such as “Breaded Nugget-Shaped Chicken Patties”. A product labeled “breaded” carries batter and breading of no more than 30 percent of the finished product. “Ice glazed” beside the name means an ice glaze set the breading. “Mechanically Separated Chicken” is poultry with most of the bone removed by machine, in a paste-like form. Its bone solids are at most 1 percent. For added fat, Kristy’s standard is tallow, olive oil, or coconut oil. Skip seed oils; avocado oil fits only when the maker states it is pure and cold-pressed.
